native.name: read_file
native.description: Read a text file. range selects 1-based lines ("120-200", "120:$", "120:+20", "-50:$" for the last 50); first_chunk starts the read at the first occurrence of that text. Paths are relative to the working directory; paths outside it only where the run's filesystem policy allows.

first_chunk.description: Start the read at the first occurrence of this text (range then counts from there).

path.description: File to read, relative to the working directory.

range.description: 1-based line range: "120-200", "120:$" (to the end), "120:+20" (20 lines from 120); negative numbers count from the end ("-50:$").

native.name: write_file
native.description: Write a text file: mode "write" (default) creates or overwrites it, "append" adds to its end, "new" creates it and fails if it exists. Parent directories are created. Paths are relative to the working directory; paths outside it only where the run's filesystem policy allows.

mode.description: `write` (default): create or overwrite; `append`: add to the end; `new`: create, fail if the file exists.

path.description: File to write, relative to the working directory.

native.name: edit_file
native.description: Replace the one exact occurrence of old_string with new_string in a text file. Fails when old_string is absent or occurs more than once: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. Paths are relative to the working directory; paths outside it only where the run's filesystem policy allows.

old_string.description: The exact text to replace; it must occur exactly once.

path.description: File to edit, relative to the working directory.

native.name: shell
native.description: Run a command in this run's runtime (native) with bash syntax. It starts in the working directory unless cwd is given; it is not sandboxed and runs with the current user's permissions. The command is a child process of this executor: an interrupt or a timeout ends its process group; processes it leaves behind after returning are not managed. Waits for the command to finish. Default timeout 1800s, max 3600s; on timeout the command is stopped and the output so far is returned. Start a long-lived service with nohup / setsid and return at once; on Unix, processes started with `&` / nohup in the foreground command's process group also end when that command is interrupted or times out. Long output keeps its beginning and end.

cwd.description: Working directory, relative to or within the configured workspace. Defaults to the workspace.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds (default 1800000, max 3600000). Set it explicitly for long builds, tests or media commands.
